turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Good morning, Mr Krishnamurthy. Before the doctor calls you, I will just check the pressure and the pulse. Please keep the arm relaxed.

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, yes, this arm only, the right one, because last time in Jayanagar they said the left side reading jumps a little, though I personally think both are the same if you sit quietly for two minutes.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is 146 over 88, pulse 78, oxygen 97 percent. I will send these in with you.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please come in, Mr Krishnamurthy, and Mrs Krishnamurthy, sit. What has brought you both today?
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, he will say he is perfectly fine. But he keeps repeating the same questions, he is forgetting appointments, and one day he got lost near the market.

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I am fine, doctor, truly. I read the newspaper front to back, I water the plants at seven, I even remember the milkman's change. My wife worries because she has too much time after retirement, that is the whole thing.

[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): So from your side you feel quite well, and from your wife's side there is worry about memory, missed appointments, and getting lost. Let me hear the details before I form any view.
[SEG0008] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Since about six months he asks me what is for lunch, I answer, and ten minutes later he asks the same thing again, sometimes three times.

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): That is not forgetting. I ask again because the menu changes, and if you say sambar now and then you make rasam, a man is allowed to confirm. I was a headmaster for thirty-two years, doctor, I do not forget a timetable.
[SEG0010] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He also missed the dentist on the 4th and the eye check after that. I had written both on the calendar.

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): The dentist himself shifted the slot, madam, I am telling you. I reached there and the girl at the desk said come next week. The eye appointment I did not forget; the traffic on Bannerghatta Road was impossible that afternoon.

[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): All right. You are saying the appointments were not forgotten, they were changed or the traffic got in the way. Your wife feels they were missed. What about the day near the market?
[SEG0013] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Last month, near Russell Market, he could not find the bus stop he has used for years. Our neighbour, Mrs Rao, brought him home in an auto.

[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): I was not lost. There was road digging near the flower shops, so I took the long way by the mosque, which I know very well. Mrs Rao simply offered a lift because it was hot, and I accepted out of politeness.

[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): So one account is that you were lost and a neighbour brought you back, and your account is that you chose a longer familiar road and accepted a lift. I will keep both, I am not deciding between them today.
[SEG0016] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He also loses the thread in conversation, and twice he could not recall our neighbour's son's name, the boy he has known since he was small.

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Names have always slipped, even when I was marking registers in 1987. There was a boy called Srinivas and another Srinivasan and I mixed them then also, so this is not a new disease, it is just how my mind files names.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long would you say this has been going on, Mr Krishnamurthy, if you had to put a time on it?

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): I cannot put a date, doctor. If my wife is insisting, maybe since Diwali or after Diwali, or was it the winter before, these festivals all blur when you are seventy-four. I am not agreeing there is a problem, I am only saying I cannot date a thing that I do not see.
[SEG0020] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): From my side it is about six months, gradual, not sudden. He is seventy-four, yes, that part is correct.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any headache, giddiness, or weakness on one side?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Headache, mm, I suppose, sometimes, not really. Only if I read too late under the tube light, and even then it is nothing I would call a headache, more like the eyes are tired, so I would not say yes.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will not record that as a headache then, it sounds too uncertain. Any chest pain, breathlessness, or falls?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain, no breathlessness, and I have not fallen. I walk to the park gate and back, slowly, but I do not fall.
[SEG0025] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No falls, that is true. He is steady on his feet. Sleep is all right also, he is not up wandering.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. Before we go to the tablets, you were saying something about your grandson as you came in?

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, Arjun, my daughter's boy, he is twelve now. He bowled four overs in the school match on Sunday and they still lost, but his line was better than last term, I sat in the sun the whole time.

[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The traffic coming back from that ground was worse than the match. We were stuck near the flyover for forty minutes, and then it rained, a proper short sharp shower.

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): And the umpire was the maths teacher, the same one who cannot add, so two wides were not given. Arjun wanted ice cream after, chocolate, and we found a shop that was still open.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sounds like a full Sunday. The monsoon showers have been sudden this week, haven't they.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, one minute sun, next minute the road is a river. My neighbour's dog hates it, he will not step out, which is funny because that dog chases every squirrel in the compound.
[SEG0032] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We should take Arjun to the Chinnaswamy one day if tickets come, he keeps asking. Anyway, that is not why we are here, sorry doctor.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not at all. Coming back to health, who looks after the tablets at home?
[SEG0034] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I do. If I leave the box with him he will take the morning ones at night. I set them out after breakfast and after dinner.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): I can manage my own tablets, doctor. I kept the school accounts for years, debit and credit, I am not going to mix up three small boxes. She hovers, that is her nature.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Which tablets are going at present?

[SEG0037] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Metformin 500 milligrams, one tablet twice a day with meals, for the sugar. And amlodipine 5 milligrams every morning for the BP. And atorvastatin 10 milligrams at night for cholesterol.

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Metformin yes, 500, with food, morning and night, that one I know. The BP tablet is not 5, doctor. The physician in Jayanagar put it up to 10 milligrams last year, I remember the conversation very clearly, he said five was not holding the pressure.
[SEG0039] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The strip in the cupboard says amlodipine 5. I have been giving 5 only. I have not seen a 10 milligram strip in the house.

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): So metformin 500 twice daily and atorvastatin 10 at night are agreed. For amlodipine, you say 10 milligrams and your wife says the strip is 5, so I will not write a dose until we see the strip. Does he actually take them as set out?

[SEG0041] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The morning ones, yes. The night metformin he sometimes skips if I am on the phone or out, and he will say he took it when the tablet is still in the box. I cannot be sure of the evenings.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): I take it. If once in a way the box still has it, that is because she herself forgot to hand it, not because I refused. I am not a child.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will note that evening metformin may be missed, and we do not know how often. Any allergy to medicines, or to foods?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): None. No medicine allergy, no food allergy. Penicillin I have taken in the past for a tooth, no rash, nothing.
[SEG0045] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Correct, no allergies that I have seen in forty-six years.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the sugar and the pressure, how long have those been there?

[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Sugar was found when I was still in service, I must have been fifty-eight or fifty-nine, they did a camp in the school. Pressure came a few years after I retired. Both are ongoing, I take the tablets, I am not cured of them, obviously.

[SEG0048] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, diabetes and high BP, both ongoing. His father, in his eighties, became very forgetful at the end, could not recognise my husband for a while. No one else in the family that I know of.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you. So longstanding diabetes and high blood pressure, both still present, and a father who had memory trouble late in life. Any operations?
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the cataract in the right eye, about eight years back, at Narayana Netralaya. Left eye they said can wait. No heart surgery, no abdomen surgery, nothing else.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Have you had blood tests recently, and did anyone give you a result?

[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, at that small lab near the temple, not the big hospital. The girl at the counter said the sugar was borderline. She did not give me a number, she just said borderline, come back if the doctor wants it repeated, and the queue was very long that day because of a wedding party all coming for dengue tests or something.
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): When was that test?

[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): I cannot date it, doctor. Last winter, or the winter before that, maybe after Diwali, maybe not. I asked them for the paper later and they said the file had been sent out. So the timing I simply do not have.
[SEG0055] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I was out of station at my sister's then, so I also cannot date it. I never saw the report. He told me borderline, that is all.

[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): So a previous blood sugar was described as borderline, with no figure, and neither of you can date it. I will not treat that as a confirmed number. Do you smoke, or take alcohol?

[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never smoked, not even in college. Alcohol, a small peg at weddings years ago, nothing now, I stopped that completely after the sugar was found. We live together, just the two of us, the daughter is in Mysore.

[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me examine you briefly. Pulse is regular, chest is clear, and there is no weakness in the arms or the legs. You were able to tell me the place and the day without difficulty.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): Tuesday, your clinic, yes. I also know the prime minister and my bank account number, if you want those, though I will not say the account number aloud in a corridor.

[SEG0060] person_3 (DOCTOR): That is enough, thank you. I am not going to put a name on this today. What I would like is a set of blood tests, sugar and HbA1c, vitamin B12, thyroid, and kidney function, and a proper memory assessment in our clinic.
[SEG0061] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So you are arranging both, the bloods and the memory assessment? Not waiting to see?

[SEG0062] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, both are arranged from today. Please also bring the amlodipine strip next time so we can settle the 5 versus 10. Keep giving the medicines as you have been, do not change the dose on your own.

[SEG0063] person_2 (PATIENT): I will bring the strip, though I am still sure it was put up to 10. And I will come for the memory thing, even if I think it is unnecessary, because my wife will not rest otherwise.

[SEG0064] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will see you again in about six weeks, once the blood results and the memory assessment are back. If anything sudden happens, weakness, confusion that is new, or a fall, come earlier or go to casualty.
[SEG0065] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Six weeks, we will be there. I will keep the calendar myself this time.
[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): Write it in two places, she will still ask me if I remember, and I will remember, doctor, you watch.
[SEG0067] person_3 (DOCTOR): We will go through it properly then. Take care on the way out, the corridor is a bit wet from the rain.
[SEG0068] person_1 (NURSE): I will book the bloods at the lab downstairs and put the memory assessment request through. You can collect the forms at the desk.

spec.situation: Spouse brings an older person who 'is fine' but repeats questions, forgets appointments and got lost; patient disagrees on many points; medicines managed by spouse; doctor plans bloods and a memory assessment, no diagnosis said aloud.
features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

omissions.text: Headache and giddiness were specifically asked about and effectively denied; patient described only occasional eye strain from reading late under a tube light and doctor said this would not be recorded as headache.
No unilateral weakness was denied in the history when asked ('Any headache, giddiness, or weakness on one side?').
Family member reported that if left to manage his own tablets, he may take the morning tablets at night; she sets them out after breakfast and after dinner.

Amlodipine dose is unresolved and the doctor explicitly said he would not write a dose until the strip is seen; recording it as a current medication without noting the dose is withheld is potentially misleading.
Penicillin was tolerated previously for a tooth with no rash, supporting the statement of no medicine allergy.
Father's late-life memory problem was described in more detail: in his eighties he became very forgetful and at times did not recognise the patient; no other family history known.
Left eye cataract has not been operated on; he was told it could wait.
Previous blood test result was only verbally described as 'borderline' sugar with no numeric value, and the doctor said he would not treat it as a confirmed number.
Examination/history noted he was able to state the day and place correctly ('Tuesday, your clinic').
Doctor stated he was not going to put a name/diagnosis on the memory issue today.

The doctor asked about headache, giddiness, or weakness on one side; the patient’s reply denied headache only unclearly, and the doctor later found no weakness in the arms or legs on exam, but the symptom screen negatives for giddiness and unilateral weakness are missing.

The recorded medication for amlodipine is incomplete/misleading because no dose should be recorded as current until the strip is checked. The wife specifically confirmed he is steady on his feet in addition to no falls; this functional observation is not recorded.

The prior blood test result was specifically described as 'borderline sugar' by the lab counter staff, not just a generic completed blood sugar test; the fact that no numeric result was available and the doctor would not treat it as a confirmed number is partly captured, but the source/detail of the 'borderline' description is not fully reflected in the investigation entry.
